verdict: ARTIFACT / NOT ON THE CRITICAL PATH. The 7.26 ms 'client<->server per-round boundary' (101.06 - 93.8) is a cross-build + cross-shape + cross-statistic arithmetic difference, not a boundary cost. Same-boot, same-request measurement (next16-instr OFF, raw/p3: client recs matched to that request's own server PROF rounds) shows client-observed ms/round sits only +0.23...+0.51 ms above the server loop's own mean per-round wall (round_total_mean + inter-round gap), for BOTH benign and agentic shapes. True client<->server per-round gap ~= 0.3-0.5 ms (delivery offset of first vs last delta in the client's decode_s window); the rest of the 7.26 decomposes into ~5.5 ms agentic-vs-benign shape (verify 97.8 vs 92.2; server round_total medians 99.23/99.28 vs 93.69/93.71) + ~0.65 ms in-engine inter-round gap + ~1.1 ms cold-first-round amortization (median excludes it) + statistic slop. The engine decode loop is a SERVER-INTERNAL generator loop that streams tokens out; the next round's dispatch is gated only on the LOCAL in-process consumer drain + a required cross-rank cancel collective — never on any client-side receipt/return. Addressable as a production lever: ~0 ms (the only recurring cross-boundary item, the 0.63-0.69 ms suspend/resume window, is in-process, contains a needed collective, and is already inside the client number).
loop_mechanism: Server-internal loop, streaming — NOT request/response-per-round. (1) Deployed DSv4.1 instance runs Dsv41Engine (src/exo/worker/engines/mlx/dsv41/engine.py), selected by model card via dsv41/dispatch.py:36-56 -> Dsv41Builder (dsv41/builder.py:89-108); batch_generate.py / speculative/dsv4_mtp.py / pp_batched_* are the OTHER (batched/PP) path and are NOT imported by the dsv41 engine (docstring-only reference at dsv41/rounds.py:124). (2) Round loop _rounds (engine.py:1027-1076): per round _check_cancel (engine.py:1047, cross-rank agreement collective) -> _one_round (engine.py:1049, DSpark draft+verify forward, dsv41/rounds.py:328-460) -> yield batch (engine.py:1075). One HTTP request -> one long SSE stream; the generator suspends at each round's yield and resumes only on the LOCAL consumer's next pull. (3) Consumer chain is all in-process: _generate/committed_tokens (engine.py:849-855) -> per-token _mid_response (engine.py:912) -> dsv41_output_parser -> _queue_of None-flush sentinel (rounds.py:115-133) -> Dsv41Engine.step() (engine.py:451-492) -> runner loop 'while self.active_tasks: results = self.generator.step()' (runner/runner.py:649-653) -> send_chunk -> event_sender.send(ChunkGenerated) (runner.py:869-884) = MpSender.send -> mp.Queue.put (utils/channels.py:260-268) into an UNBOUNDED queue (mp_channel default max_buffer_size=inf -> mp.Queue(0), channels.py:222-231,442-455), so send never blocks on space; supervisor forwards events to master from a separate async task (_forward_events, runner/supervisor.py:844-886). Client/HTTP/SSE sits behind master in other processes and CANNOT gate the worker decode loop. (4) Measured inter-round in-engine gap (suspend at round k's yield -> resume for round k+1's compute; derived from next16 PROF emit_ms being cumulative-from-loop-start: Delta(emit) - round_total_{k-1}; both ranks agree): median 0.63-0.69 ms, mean 0.62-0.68 — contains detokenize/parse/send drain + the _check_cancel collective (mx_any/all_sum+eval, utils_mlx.py:2147-2154) + per-token step-loop overhead across the ~3.5 committed tokens of the round. (5) t/s: the server's own generation_tps is structurally 0.0 on this engine (the : generation_stats frame carries the field but _RoundStats (engine.py:263) is never instantiated/passed — _final_response called without round_stats at engine.py:898-910/920 -> rounds.py:213 else-branch -> generation_tps=0.0, rounds.py:222-231; confirmed 0.0 in every live frame, raw/p3/levers_off_recs.jsonl + raw/p3b/next17h0_agentic.json.jsonl). ALL published t/s + ms/round are client stats: decode_tps=(completion_tokens-1)/decode_s, ms_per_round=decode_s*1000/(d_cycles/3), decode_s = wall between first and last decoded content/reasoning SSE delta, rounds = server counter read from the stats frame (phase19_round_measure.py:96-105,120-135; phase19_agentic_measure.py:201-217,248-263; p3b_driver.py:36-77,122). So the honest production per-round number IS the client-observed one (94.94/99.46 live), already within ~+0.2...+2.4 ms of the engine's own same-boot numbers for every server statistic choice (loop wall/n +0.23...+0.51; round_total mean +0.9...+1.1; round_total median +1.2...+2.4).
